:::{#thm-kraft-inequality}
#### Kraft's inequality

Let $X$ be a [discrete random variable](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-discrete-rv) that takes a finite number of values,
and let a [prefix code](#def-prefix-code) for $X$ have [codeword lengths](source-coding.qmd#def-code) $\ell(x)$.
Then

$$\sum_x 2^{-\ell(x)} \le 1.$$

:::

::: {.proof}

Let $m$ be the largest codeword length, which exists because $X$ takes a finite number of values.
For each value $x$, the strings of $m$ [bits](entropy.qmd#def-bit) that start with the codeword $c(x)$
are those that choose the remaining $m - \ell(x)$ bits freely,
so there are $2^{m - \ell(x)}$ of them.

No string of $m$ bits starts with two different codewords.
If it started with $c(x)$ and with $c(x')$, where $\ell(x) \le \ell(x')$,
then $c(x)$ would be the first $\ell(x)$ bits of $c(x')$,
which the [prefix code](#def-prefix-code) forbids.
So the sets of strings that start with different codewords do not overlap.

There are $2^m$ strings of $m$ bits in all, so the sets together hold at most that many:

$$\sum_x 2^{m - \ell(x)} \le 2^m.$$

Dividing both sides by $2^m$ gives the inequality.

:::
